chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Abra ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man hears the testimony and is not called upon to testify against it, if he wishes he may testify, and if he wishes he may remain silent.

key_terms.يُشْهَدْ: To be called upon to testify

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who hears testimony but is not called to testify?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*’s chapter on proofs, this hadith clarifies the distinction between general knowledge and formal legal testimony (*bayyinah*), establishing that mere hearing does not create an obligatory duty (*wujub*) to testify. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that testimony requires a specific summons or clear requirement, protecting individuals from being compelled to bear witness without explicit cause. It underscores the precision in Islamic legal procedure regarding the transition from private knowledge to public legal evidence.
